result.scope_note: The claim refers to the HTTP/1.1 specification as standardized in RFC 9110 (June 2022), specifically the definitions of 'safe' and 'idempotent' methods. The standard applies globally, so no regional variation is expected.

explanation.text: RFC 9110, published in June 2022, defines the safe HTTP methods as GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, and TRACE in Section 9.2.1.
Section 9.2.2 of RFC 9110 states that the safe request methods, along with PUT and DELETE, are idempotent.
The claim refers to the worldwide standard as of June 2022, which is accurately represented by RFC 9110.

assessment.rationale: Spans state RFC 9110 (June 2022) defines safe HTTP methods and classifies them as idempotent; supports the claim that every safe method is idempotent per the standard.
assessment.synthesis_coverage: Covers classification of safe methods as idempotent in RFC 9110 (June 2022)

excerpts.text:
RFC 9110 section 9 defines eight methods and classifies each as safe (read only in intent) and idempotent (repeating it has the same intended effect as sending it once):

| Method | Purpose | Safe | Idempotent |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
RFC 9110 explains that idempotent requests "can be repeated automatically if a communication failure occurs", and that a proxy "MUST NOT automatically retry non-idempotent requests".
